benchmarks.task_description:
zypper_repository: keep `description` when adding a `.repo` file

##### SUMMARY
When adding a `.repo` file, the `name` value from the file overrode the `description` option, so the name zypper displays for the repository could not be set. The `description` is now passed to zypper whenever it is set.

The docs of `name` are also clarified: it is the repository alias, which cannot be set for `.repo` files (zypper takes it from the file). The name displayed by zypper (`zypper addrepo --name`) is set with `description`.

```yaml
- community.general.zypper_repository:
    repo: https://packages.microsoft.com/config/sles/15/prod.repo
    description: microsoft-prod
```

Fixes #4532

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bugfix Pull Request
- Docs Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
zypper_repository

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
AI (Claude Code) was used to assist with this contribution.

benchmarks.task_description:
Bugfix: archive storage could replace a hand-built code environment

* With code-environment-storage = archive, updating a plug-in's code built an archive from the plug-in's environment file for whatever environment the code's .ini file names -- even one SEAMM did not make, such as a hand-built environment for a particular PyTorch or code build. Every job would then have run in the plug-in's standard environment instead. Such environments are now left alone, as they already were with directory storage.

(Found while switching ARC to archive storage: lammps.ini and xnn.ini there name the hand-built seamm-lammps-xnn0240. The switch converted only the six environments SEAMM made, so nothing was replaced.)

fix(review): use the prepared diff when packing yields one chunk ### **User description** ## Problem With `pr_reviewer.enable_large_pr_chunking=true`, an oversized file may be omitted from the initial diff even when the chunk packer produces one usable chunk. The reviewer discards that chunk, leaving only filename context rather than source changes. ## Changes - Review the single prepared chunk and preserve its partial/remaining-file coverage. - Replan fallback attempts for each model's token budget; use the full diff when a fallback can fit it. - Retain deleted-file notices within the final rendered request budget without displacing usable source content. - Keep single-call progress, publishing behavior, and existing configuration unchanged. ## Validation - Regression coverage for clipped single chunks, different fallback budgets, and empty chunk plans. - Related tests, complete unit suite, Ruff, and pre-commit checks passed. ## Trade-off Restoring source coverage can increase input tokens; large-PR chunking remains opt-in. ___ ### **PR Type** Bug fix, Tests ___ ### **Description** - Review prepared single chunks with accurate coverage. - Replan fallbacks using model-specific token budgets. - Preserve deleted-file notices without overflowing prompts. - Test clipping, fallback budgets, and empty plans. ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Prepared diff and coverage"] B["Model-specific chunk plan"] C["Single chunk with budgeted metadata"] D["Single-call review"] E["Cached multi-chunk review"] F["Fallback model budget"] A --> B B -- "One chunk" --> C C --> D B -- "Multiple chunks" --> E D -- "Fallback needed" --> F F -- "Replan" --> A ```

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(github): resolve the actual PR head when commit lists are truncated

## Problem

GitHub's pull-request commits endpoint returns at most 250 commits. For larger PRs, its final listed commit can differ from `pr.head.sha`. Using that tail as the latest commit can attach check runs and latest-commit links to an older SHA.

## Change

- Reuse the last listed commit when its SHA matches the PR head.
- Otherwise look up the declared head SHA, including when the list is empty.
- Keep the commit list unchanged and fail rather than use a stale head if the lookup fails.
- Avoid an extra request for ordinary PRs whose listed tail already matches.

## Tests

Extend the existing provider tests for empty, matching, mismatched, and 250/251-commit lists; verify check-run targets, latest-commit URLs, and snapshot preservation on failed refresh.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: replace a dropped song from the round-cap reserve instead of shortening the game (#3441)

Refs #3441 (addresses the "game ends early" part; the slow Music Assistant starts themselves are not changed here, see below)

## What changed
When a song is dropped (no URI for the provider, or a start that did not land within the budget), the game used to lower `total_rounds` straight away (#3279). With a round cap, the playlist's remaining songs sit in the reserve (#2547), so the game was shortened even though plenty of songs were left. In the #3441 log a 98-song playlist capped at 10 rounds lost four rate-limited starts and ended after round 6.

New `_replace_dropped_song()` in `game/state_lifecycle.py` first releases one reserve song (`next_up=True`, same as the host's song swap in #3321, so a ramp-up finale keeps its place). Only when the reserve is empty does it fall back to the #3279 accounting. Both drop paths (failed start, no URI) use it.

## Readiness assessment
- [ ] Ready to merge
- [x] Borderline — see notes
- [ ] Not ready — needs human review

**Honest summary:** The change is small and mirrors what the song swap already does. It deliberately reverses one assertion from #3321 (`test_failed_song_still_lowers_total_rounds`, now `test_failed_song_is_replaced_from_the_reserve`): a failed song in a capped game no longer costs a round while the reserve has songs. It does not shorten the 22–31 s waits or stop slow-but-playable songs from being skipped; those come from Music Assistant's Spotify rate limiter and need a separate decision.

## Test plan
- `tests/unit/test_dropped_song_refill_3441.py`: capped game keeps `total_rounds == 10` after an `unavailable` or `rate_limited` drop and draws one song from the reserve; an uncapped game still drops to 4 of 5.
- Full suite: `pytest tests/unit tests/integration` (3445 passed), `npm test` (2611 passed), `npm run build:check`, ruff 0.17.3 format/check on touched files.
- Manual: MA + Spotify game with 10 rounds on a larger playlist; force a skipped start and check the counter stays "of 10" and the game plays 10 rounds.

## Risk assessment
- **Blast radius:** round-start skip path in `game/state_lifecycle.py` only.
- **What could go wrong:** in a capped game where most tracks fail (e.g. a storefront gap), the game now walks into the reserve instead of ending early, so each extra failed start can add up to 25 s of waiting. Uncapped games already behaved this way. The "rate_limited"/"error" path still pauses after two failures in a row, so a dead speaker or provider still reaches the recovery banner. Fewer reserve songs are left for the encore and the finale playoff.
- **What I did NOT test:** a live game against Music Assistant; ramp-up ordering with a drop in a live game (covered only by the shared `next_up` path the swap already uses).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
